e01-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e01-00-problem-l01-sam.text: One coin costs that much? I can't even afford a ticket in.

e01-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e01-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: That's the price of one whole coin. It's not what you have to pay each time. Bitcoin is a digital asset, and you can hold it in decimal amounts. You usually don't buy a whole one.

e01-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e01-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: One practice sum. Say one bitcoin is 50,000 USDT and you spend 100. Ignoring fees, that's 0.002 bitcoin. This is not today's market price.

e01-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e01-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: The number of coins can stay the same, but their value goes up and down. Buying a little means risking less. It doesn't mean no risk.

e01-05-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e01-05-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: You can split it, but not every platform accepts any tiny order. Check the minimum amount and the fees. While you learn, use virtual funds. No deposit needed.

e01-06-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e01-06-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Do you have to buy a whole bitcoin? No. Remember: the price of one coin is not the price of getting started.

e01-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e01-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: Most trades are priced in USDT. But is USDT really a dollar? Next episode.

e02-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e02-00-problem-l01-sam.text: It's called Tether, so it's basically dollars in the bank, right?

e02-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e02-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: No. USDT, or Tether, is a stablecoin. It's designed to stay close to one dollar. But it isn't the dollars in your bank account, and it isn't risk-free cash.

e02-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e02-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Exchanges often use it to price and swap assets. You might buy bitcoin with USDT, and when you sell, you may get USDT back, not a bank transfer.

e02-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e02-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: 'Stable' is a design goal, not a guarantee. The price can drift, and issuing and redeeming come with conditions. If you hold it, learn about the issuer and the platform risks too.

e02-05-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e02-05-lesson-l01-sam.text: So I have to buy USDT before bitcoin?

e02-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e02-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Not always. Which currencies and trading pairs you can use depends on your region and your platform.

e02-06-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e02-06-lesson-l01-narrator.text: What's wrong with this sentence? A stablecoin is not a promise to protect your money. Know what it's for, and know it can be unstable.

e02-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e02-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: If your phone breaks tonight, are your coins gone too? Next: where your coins actually live.

e03-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e03-00-problem-l01-sam.text: My phone broke. Are my coins smashed too?

e03-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e03-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Your coins aren't inside your phone. A wallet lets you see assets on the blockchain and uses keys to approve actions. Whether you can recover depends on the wallet type and the recovery options you kept.

e03-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e03-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: With a custodial exchange account, the platform mainly manages the assets and keys, and you act through your account. With a self-custody wallet, you control the credentials. Convenience and responsibility are split differently.

e03-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e03-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: Forget your password on either one, and you just call support?

e03-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e03-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Don't think of it that way. With a standard recovery-phrase wallet, if you lose the phrase and have no other valid recovery method, support can't get it back for you.

e03-05-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e03-05-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Keeping assets on a platform carries platform risk. Holding them yourself can go wrong through a leaked key or a bad approval. Today, just understand the difference. You don't need to move everything right now.

e03-06-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e03-06-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Who controls the permission to move the assets? Answer that first. Then decide which account or wallet you need.

e03-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e03-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: Two doors look the same. One is fake. Next episode: how to spot the real one.

e04-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e04-00-problem-l01-sam.text: This one has a huge reward. I'll just go in here?

e04-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e04-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Don't let a reward decide. First check: is this allowed where you live? Does the platform accept your real country of residence? Which company provides the service? Then look at fees, deposits and withdrawal rules.

e04-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e04-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Once you've confirmed the official entry, sign up with your own email or phone number, set a unique password, and complete the checks the page asks for. Never buy someone else's account, and never fake your identity or region.

e04-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e04-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Signing up isn't the last step. Turn on the security features the platform supports, check your logged-in devices, and save your recovery options. And never send a one-time code to a so-called support agent.

e04-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e04-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Our site can help you look things up, but a partnership is not a safety guarantee. If the facts aren't confirmed, don't start the sign-up.

e04-06-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e04-06-lesson-l01-sam.text: Stop. Confirm eligibility and the rules first.

e04-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e04-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Right. Find the real door, then open the account.

e04-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e04-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.text: Want a door you can trust? NexuAlpha lists each exchange's verified official link. Our OKX partner link goes straight to the official site, and code nexu888 adds a fee rebate.

e04-08-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e04-08-hook-l01-narrator.text: Do it now: turn on two-factor login. Then come back. Next, someone in a chat offers to 'do your KYC for you'.

e05-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e05-00-problem-l01-sam.text: It wants my ID. And this guy says he can do it for me?

e05-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e05-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Identity checks are usually there to confirm you are the account owner and to meet the rules. Make sure it's the official flow first. Don't hand your ID or codes to an 'agent' in a chat group.

e05-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e05-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Usually you enter your real details, upload a supported valid ID, then follow the prompts for a photo or face check. Whether you need proof of address, and which IDs are accepted, depends on your region and platform.

e05-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e05-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: If it fails, read the reason first. Is the ID expired? Is there glare? Does the name match? Fix it as instructed. Never try again with a fake identity.

e05-05-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e05-05-lesson-l01-sam.text: Once I'm done, can I trade right away?

e05-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e05-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Not guaranteed. The result, the products you can use and whether you can deposit all depend on the official notice. And this academy never collects your real ID.

e05-06-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e05-06-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Who gets your ID? Only the verified official flow. Not us, and not a stranger.

e05-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e05-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.text: Ready to verify? Start only on the official site. Our OKX partner link takes you straight there, with code nexu888 for a fee rebate. We never ask for your ID.

e05-08-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e05-08-hook-l01-narrator.text: Deposit, buy, transfer: three buttons that all look the same. Next: which one to press.

e06-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e06-00-problem-l01-sam.text: These all look like putting money in. Which one do I press?

e06-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e06-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Start with what you're holding. Money in your bank, coins you already have somewhere else, or a balance in another account on the same platform. Each one takes a different route.

e06-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e06-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: A fiat deposit usually adds a cash balance to your account. Buying crypto directly means you pay and receive a crypto asset. Some platforms support bank or card channels, some don't, and fees and limits differ.

e06-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e06-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: If you already hold crypto, you can deposit it using a supported coin and network. An internal transfer just moves balance between your accounts. It's usually not an on-chain transfer. Check where the balance will land first.

e06-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e06-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Some platforms also offer trading between users. That's not another name for a bank transfer. Never pay off-platform in private, never use funds of unknown origin or third-party payments. If it's unclear, don't do it yet.

e06-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e06-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Right. Look at the asset first, then the route, and finally check what actually arrived.

e06-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e06-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: BTC/USDT: does that slash mean you buy two coins? Next: your first spot trade.

e07-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e07-00-problem-l01-sam.text: This slash. Do I have to buy both coins?

e07-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e07-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: No. It means bitcoin is priced in USDT. When you buy, you pay USDT and get bitcoin. When you sell, it goes the other way.

e07-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e07-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: We practise with a virtual account. Make sure it's spot, not futures. Pick the pair, choose Buy, then enter the amount. Before you submit, check whether the box wants an amount of money or a number of coins.

e07-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e07-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Say the fill price is 50,000 and you spend 100. You get 0.002 bitcoin. Now assume a 0.1% fee taken separately from your USDT. You spend 100.10 in total. Real rules depend on the platform.

e07-05-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e07-05-lesson-l01-sam.text: So once I tap Buy, I definitely have the coins?

e07-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e07-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Check the trade history too. Not filled, partly filled and fully filled are different. Check the real average price and the fee as well.

e07-06-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e07-06-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Your first practice isn't about guessing up or down. It's about checking these five things. And when you're done, it's fine to not make a real trade yet.

e07-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e07-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.text: When you're ready for a real first trade, open Bitget through our partner link. Code nexu888 gets part of your trading fees back. Same five checks, every time.

e07-08-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e07-08-hook-l01-narrator.text: Say the price rises and you sell. So why is your bank balance still the same? Next episode.

e08-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e08-00-problem-l01-sam.text: I definitely sold. So why hasn't my bank got the money?

e08-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e08-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Check which pair you sold into. If you sold for USDT, you got a USDT balance, not money in the bank. Selling and withdrawing to your bank are two separate steps.

e08-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e08-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Same teaching example. You sell 0.002 bitcoin at 55,000. That's 110. Take off an assumed fee of 0.11, and 109.89 lands in your account.

e08-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e08-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Take off the costs. Here it's 9.79, before any currency conversion or withdrawal fees. A price going up isn't the same as your final net gain.

e08-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e08-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: If you need the money back in your bank, first check that your region supports it. Then convert or withdraw through the official route to an account in your own name. Check the name, the amount received, the fees and the processing conditions.

e08-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e08-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Keep your trade and withdrawal records. If you're not sure what kind of balance it is, don't decide based on one 'success' message.

e08-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e08-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: One cheaper network. One wrong click. Your coins may never arrive. Next: the checks you never guess.

e09-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e09-00-problem-l01-sam.text: This network is cheaper. Why not just switch?

e09-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e09-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: First confirm which asset and network the receiver supports. Then think about fees. If the two ends don't match, don't send just because it's cheaper. Even USDT can live on different networks.

e09-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e09-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: For now, think of the network as the route and the address as the destination. But two addresses can look alike and still not work on the same network. Always check that the receiving platform supports this chain and this asset.

e09-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e09-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Copy the address from the receiving page, then check all of it. If a memo or tag is required, fill it in. Confirm the minimum deposit, the withdrawal fee and the amount that will arrive. Don't judge an address by its first and last few characters.

e09-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e09-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Send a small test that meets the minimum, and confirm it was actually credited. For a bigger transfer, check everything again. Don't blindly reuse old records. For self-custody transfers, have the network fee ready too.

e09-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e09-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: One more check before sending beats looking for help after a mistake.

e09-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e09-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: It says 'success', but nothing arrived. Don't send it again. Next: where to look.

e10-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e10-00-problem-l01-sam.text: It didn't arrive. Should I just send a few more?

e10-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e10-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Don't send again. Submitted, on-chain and credited are not the same thing. Find which station it's stuck at, then decide who to contact.

e10-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e10-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Keep the send record. If there's a transaction hash, check it on a proper block explorer for that network: status, destination address and amount. Don't mix in results from a different chain.

e10-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e10-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: The receiving platform may still need confirmations or an internal review. If the coin, network, address or memo was wrong, stop sending and give the facts to official support.

e10-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e10-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: A completed on-chain transfer usually can't be undone like a normal action. Whether it can be recovered depends on technical and platform conditions. There's no guarantee. Don't believe anyone who says paying a fee will surely get it back.

e10-06-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e10-06-lesson-l01-sam.text: Give the records they need. Never the recovery phrase, private key or codes.

e10-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e10-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Right. Find where it's stuck first. Don't keep sending.

e10-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e10-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: 'Hi, I'm support. Send me your recovery phrase.' Next: what scammers really want.

e11-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e11-00-problem-l01-sam.text: He says he's support and he'll upgrade my wallet.

e11-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e11-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: For a standard recovery-phrase wallet, the phrase is the control key, not a support code. Same for your private key. Never send them to anyone. Even our academy assistant should never ask for them.

e11-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e11-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Two more danger signs: guaranteed returns, and pressure to pay. A screenshot of big profits proves nothing, and doesn't mean you could repeat it. If someone rushes you past the normal checks, stop.

e11-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e11-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Connecting a wallet, signing a message and approving access to your assets are different things. If you don't understand a signature or approval, don't confirm it. No password prompt doesn't mean no risk.

e11-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e11-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: If you think something leaked, stop and use the official security channel. Act on what actually leaked. Never install remote-control software because a scammer told you to.

e11-06-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e11-06-lesson-l01-sam.text: Sharing info to receive money isn't the same as handing over the keys.

e11-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e11-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Share no secrets. Approve nothing you don't understand. Don't be rushed into paying.

e11-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e11-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: Eleven episodes done. Is it time to deposit real money? The Season 1 finale has a surprising answer.

e12-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e12-00-problem-l01-sam.text: I've watched eleven episodes. Should I deposit now?

e12-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e12-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Learning how doesn't mean you have to invest. Today, with practice money only, we'll run one flow: check the entry and eligibility, find spot, confirm the amount and fee, then check the trade record.

e12-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e12-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Even if the price falls in practice, you can still do everything right. We score whether you checked and understood, not whether you happened to pick a rise.

e12-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e12-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: Something's wrong with this transfer. I'm not sending it.

e12-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e12-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: That's a correct answer too. When the network, fees or identity aren't clear, stopping matters more than forcing the task through.

e12-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e12-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Finally, say three things back. Where did the asset go? How much was actually taken? Who controls your account? If you can't explain one, go back to that episode and practise again.

e12-06-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e12-06-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: What you've earned is a learning record, not a licence to invest. Keep learning, or don't trade for now. Both are fine. Understand first, then act.

e12-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e12-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.text: When you do decide to start, compare exchanges side by side on NexuAlpha. Register through an official partner link with our code, get part of your fees back, and join our Telegram for new lessons.

e12-08-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e12-08-hook-l01-narrator.text: Season 2: the price on your screen isn't always the price you pay. Find out why.

e13-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e13-00-problem-l01-sam.text: It was this price a second ago. Why is my bill different?

e13-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e13-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: The last price on screen is a record of the most recent trade. It's not an offer for unlimited size. How much people want to buy and sell right now is in the order book.

e13-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e13-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Say you buy 0.002 bitcoin. The first level only has half. The other half fills at a higher price. Together, the average is 50,050, not 50,000.

e13-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e13-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Slippage is the gap between the price you expected and the price you got. It isn't always against you. The trading fee is a separate cost. Don't lump them together under a 'free' slogan.

e13-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e13-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Bigger orders, thinner depth or fast markets make it more likely the result drifts from what you expected. Check size and depth before you order, and the real average price after.

e13-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e13-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: You only know your fill when you see the bill. Don't just watch the biggest number.

e13-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e13-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.text: Fees are one cost you can actually lower. Compare fees on NexuAlpha, and register through an official partner link with our code to get part of your trading fees back. Lower cost, same risk.

e13-08-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e13-08-hook-l01-narrator.text: You placed a buy order and nothing happens. Is it broken? Next: market, limit and cancel.

e14-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e14-00-problem-l01-sam.text: I hit Buy. Why isn't it filling?

e14-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e14-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: A market order tries to fill quickly at the prices available now, but the final price can move. A limit order says 'buy no higher' or 'sell no lower' than a set price. It isn't guaranteed to fill.

e14-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e14-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: If you want to buy below the current price, you may have to wait. On the other hand, a limit order that already meets the other side's price can fill right away. Not every limit order has to wait in line.

e14-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e14-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: So does cancelling undo what I already bought?

e14-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e14-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: No. Cancel only affects the part that hasn't filled. What already filled stays. It doesn't rewind.

e14-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e14-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Read the status before you act. Whether you're the maker or the taker depends on how the trade actually filled. Choosing 'limit' doesn't automatically get you a certain fee.

e14-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e14-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Choosing an order type is choosing how it executes. It's not making a wish.

e14-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e14-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: A green candle. Does it mean the next one goes up too? Next episode.

e15-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e15-00-problem-l01-sam.text: Green means it keeps going up next, right?

e15-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e15-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: One candle records four prices for one period: open, high, low and close. This is made-up five-minute data. It's not a promise about the next five minutes.

e15-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e15-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: The body shows the gap between open and close. The wicks mark the highest and lowest prices in that period. A candle that hasn't finished yet keeps changing with new trades.

e15-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e15-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: Why does the chart look different when I switch the time frame?

e15-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e15-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Each candle now covers a different length of time. Read the time frame first, then the shape. Don't mistake five minutes for a day.

e15-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e15-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Apps may use different colours for up and down, so read the legend and the numbers. Past moves can be informative, but one candle can't guarantee the next move.

e15-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e15-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Read the record first. Don't treat a record as a prophecy.

e15-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e15-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: 'I have 1,000 and only want to risk 20. So I go all in?' Next: how much to buy.

e16-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e16-00-problem-l01-sam.text: I have 1,000 and only want to lose 20. So I just put it all in?

e16-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e16-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: What's in your account, how much you buy in this trade, and the most you plan to lose are three different things. Decide your exit first. Then you can size the position.

e16-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e16-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: One practice sum. Entry at 50,000, planned exit at 47,500. That's 5% away. If you plan to take a 20 price loss, ignoring costs, the position is about 400.

e16-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e16-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: So 'lose at most 20' doesn't mean 'buy only 20'?

e16-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e16-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Right. Here a 400 position falling 5% is the 20. These are teaching numbers only.

e16-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e16-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Real markets have slippage, gaps, fees and failed orders, so planned risk is not a guaranteed maximum loss. Never borrow money for this course, and never practise with money you need to live on.

e16-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e16-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Work out the worst you can accept first. Then ask whether you need this trade at all.

e16-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e16-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: You set a stop-loss. Does that mean you can only lose that amount? Next: the truth about stops.

e17-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e17-00-problem-l01-sam.text: My stop-loss is set, so I can only lose the amount I typed, right?

e17-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e17-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: A stop-loss runs your exit plan when a condition is met. It's not insurance. Being triggered doesn't mean you'll fill at that price, and it doesn't guarantee the loss stops exactly there.

e17-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e17-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: After the trigger, a stop-market order exits at market. It prioritises getting out fast, but the price can slip. In fast or thin markets, the gap can be bigger.

e17-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e17-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: A stop-limit posts a limit order after the trigger. It caps the price you'll accept, but if the price races past, it may not sell at all. Neither one is always better. They're different trade-offs.

e17-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e17-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: After setting them, check the direction, quantity and order status. For futures, also check which price triggers it, so your stop isn't placed where liquidation could come first.

e17-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e17-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Know its limits, and a stop-loss becomes a real plan, not a lucky charm.

e17-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e17-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: Both say BTC. But one may not give you any bitcoin at all. Next: spot vs futures.

e18-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e18-00-problem-l01-sam.text: They both say bitcoin. Isn't it the same trade?

e18-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e18-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Plain spot, with no borrowing, swaps one asset for another. The linear perpetual we cover here is a contract position that settles profit and loss as the price moves. It's not buying bitcoin you can withdraw.

e18-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e18-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Going long usually means hoping the price rises. Going short usually means hoping it falls. Get the direction wrong, and either side loses. Being able to short doesn't make it easier to make money.

e18-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e18-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: Should I level up from spot to futures?

e18-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e18-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: No need. Futures are a different risk structure, not a level you must reach. You can understand them and still choose not to use them.

e18-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e18-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Plain spot without borrowing has no margin liquidation like futures do. But the asset can still lose a lot of value. No liquidation doesn't mean your money is protected.

e18-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e18-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Know what you're trading first. Then study leverage.

e18-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e18-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: 10x leverage: does the exchange hand you 900 extra? Next episode.

e19-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e19-00-problem-l01-sam.text: If I use ten times, does the exchange give me 900?

e19-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e19-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: It's not free cash. Simply put, 100 of margin controlling a 1,000 position is 10x leverage. Price moves act on the position, and your margin takes the profit or loss.

e19-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e19-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Ignoring fees, a 1% move against you loses about 10 on a 1,000 position, and about 20 on a 2,000 position. The percentage looks small, but on a small margin it can hurt.

e19-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e19-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Here's an easy mistake. If the position size stays the same and you only change the leverage setting, the P&L in money for the same price move doesn't double. What changes is the margin required and your risk buffer.

e19-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e19-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Real liquidation also involves maintenance margin, the mark price and fees. You can't say 10x always liquidates at exactly a 10% drop. Don't use this shortcut for real trades.

e19-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e19-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: It magnifies how the position hits your money, not your judgement.

e19-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e19-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: You still have margin left. So why can you be forced out? Next: the line you can't see.

e20-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e20-00-problem-l01-sam.text: There's still money there. Why won't it let me keep waiting?

e20-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e20-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: You need initial margin to open a position. While it's open, you must also meet the maintenance margin requirement. What you put in at the start isn't how much buffer you'll always have.

e20-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e20-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Say the initial margin is 100 and the position is down 20. Ignoring everything else, the equity is now 80. If the price keeps moving against you, the buffer keeps shrinking.

e20-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e20-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: When equity gets close to the platform's maintenance level, the risk system may step in. It doesn't have to wait for zero. It depends on the account type, margin mode and product rules.

e20-05-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e20-05-lesson-l01-sam.text: So if I keep adding money, I'm safe?

e20-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e20-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Adding money doesn't change the price direction, and it doesn't guarantee you won't be liquidated. It can pull more money into the same risk.

e20-06-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e20-06-lesson-l01-sam.text: No. One is about opening the position. The other is about keeping it open.

e20-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e20-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Check equity first, then how far it is from the warning line.

e20-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e20-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: Put 100 in a box. Is the other 900 safe forever? Next: isolated margin.

e21-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e21-00-problem-l01-sam.text: If I put 100 in isolated, the other 900 can never be touched?

e21-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e21-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Isolated margin means a position gets its own margin. In a simple setup, with no adding and no auto-add, this position's liquidation risk is mainly carried by the margin you assigned.

e21-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e21-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: So it helps you separate the margin of different positions. But that 100 can still be lost. Isolated margin doesn't make losses disappear, and it isn't a stop-loss order.

e21-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e21-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Watch this switch. Some platforms offer auto-add margin. Turn it on, and your available balance can keep flowing into the position. Adding margin by hand does the same. More money ends up carrying the risk.

e21-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e21-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Don't see the word 'isolated' and assume the most you can lose is always that first 100. Check the add-margin settings, the fees and the product rules.

e21-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e21-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: With isolated margin, look at the walls, and also at any pipes plugged into the box.

e21-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e21-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: One position leaks, and another one starts sinking. Next: cross margin.

e22-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e22-00-problem-l01-sam.text: The loss is on the left one. Why is the right one in danger too?

e22-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e22-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Cross margin shares margin across positions, within what the rules allow. Here, say one margin pool holds 1,000. Several positions may depend on it, not just on what each was first assigned.

e22-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e22-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: One losing position can eat the buffer other positions rely on. Profits, losses, margin held for open orders, and the value of your collateral can all affect the same account's risk.

e22-04-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e22-04-lesson-l01-sam.text: So cross margin is harder to liquidate, which makes it safer?

e22-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e22-04-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Extra money can delay when one position hits risk handling. But it also puts more of your money on the line for the losses.

e22-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e22-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Cross margin doesn't let a platform automatically use all your bank cards or personal wallets. Which accounts and collateral count depends on the product rules. Complex collateral can also come with haircuts and its own price risk.

e22-06-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e22-06-lesson-l01-sam.text: Not necessarily. It depends on the shared pool and the account rules.

e22-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e22-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: Look at the whole pool, not just one position's box.

e22-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e22-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: The price you watch hasn't hit the line, but the alarm is ringing. Next: who presses the liquidation button.

e23-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e23-00-problem-l01-sam.text: The price I'm watching hasn't got there. Why is the alarm going off?

e23-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e23-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: The last traded price isn't always the price used to judge liquidation. Many perpetuals assess risk using a mark price and margin rules. Check which rules your platform actually uses.

e23-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e23-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: When the price moves against the position, losses eat into equity. Near the maintenance requirement, the system may cancel orders, reduce the position or force-close it. It won't necessarily wait for your OK.

e23-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e23-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Liquidation usually means this forced-close risk event, not your phone's button breaking. The real trigger depends on fees, maintenance margin, margin mode and more. 10x doesn't mean exactly a 10% drop.

e23-05-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e23-05-lesson-l01-sam.text: It went back up later. Can I just wait for it to come back?

e23-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e23-05-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: A closed position doesn't come back on its own. A drop and then a rise can end very differently for a leveraged position and for plain spot you just held.

e23-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e23-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: It's not just the destination. It's whether you can survive the path.

e23-07-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e23-07-hook-l01-narrator.text: Price barely moved, and you didn't close, but your balance dropped. The final episode is next.

e24-00-problem-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e24-00-problem-l01-sam.text: The price barely moved and I didn't close. Why is my balance lower?

e24-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e24-02-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: Besides trading fees, perpetual contracts usually have a funding mechanism. When the rate is positive, longs usually pay shorts. When it's negative, it flips. It's not a fixed interest everyone pays to the exchange.

e24-03-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e24-03-lesson-l01-narrator.text: Say the position value at settlement is 1,000 and the rate is 0.01%. This fee is 0.10. It's based on the position value, not your first 100 of margin.

e24-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e24-04-lesson-l01-nexubo.text: The interval and the rate can change by pair, platform and market. Don't remember it as 'every contract, every eight hours, forever'. And don't treat receiving funding as risk-free income.

e24-05-lesson-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e24-05-lesson-l01-narrator.text: The last level is practice only. First explain what you're trading and which direction. Then check the mode, size, margin, auto-add, exit plan and costs. If you don't understand one item, pause. Don't guess your way through the buttons.

e24-06-lesson-l01-sam.speaker: sam
e24-06-lesson-l01-sam.text: I know how to do it, and I know this risk isn't right for me. So I won't.

e24-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e24-06-lesson-l02-nexubo.text: That's a passing result too. Finishing the course doesn't mean you can make money. Understand first, then act.

e24-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.speaker: nexubo
e24-07-conversion-l01-nexubo.text: Whatever you trade, fees are a cost that adds up. Compare fees on NexuAlpha, and register through an official partner link with our code to get part of your fees back. Lower cost, same risk.

e24-08-hook-l01-narrator.speaker: narrator
e24-08-hook-l01-narrator.text: You've finished both seasons. Pick the episode that felt hardest, and rewatch it before you ever trade.
